intervention_label: Diagnostic gates: comprehensive tissue NGS (KRAS A59T VAF + extended RAS + BRAF V600 + ERBB2 amp + TP53 R273 substitution + PIK3CA M1043I + SMAD4 + 20q segment) + HER2 IHC/FISH (HERACLES scoring) + MMR IHC + TMB mut/Mb + PD-L1 CPS + DPYD/UGT1A1 germline + Signatera baseline pre-CRS
expected_benefit: Resolves seven downstream decision gates in a single archival-block send-out plus blood draws: anti-EGFR eligibility (KRAS A59T VAF + full RAS + BRAF V600), tucatinib + trastuzumab / T-DXd (HER2 amplification), inavolisib (PIK3CA M1043I somatic + clonal), ICI doors (MMR by IHC orthogonal to NGS-MSI; TMB mut/Mb on F1CDx for the >=10 cutoff; PD-L1 clone + CPS), fluoropyrimidine + irinotecan dosing (DPYD CPIC variants + UGT1A1 *28/*6), and the peri-HIPEC recurrence-surveillance lead time (Signatera bracketing the CRS-HIPEC window with a clean baseline draw before surgery). Without these, every downstream pick has to hedge on biomarker status.
key_risks: Negligible — archival FFPE block release + EDTA peripheral blood draw + a pre-op Signatera draw; no fresh biopsy and no patient-facing toxicity.
preference_alignment: Matches the 'surface the full option space' free-text framing: every downstream pick is biomarker-conditional, so the gates have to land first; matches the trial-prefer preference because INTRINSIC, RASolve-GI, and DESTINY-CRC02-class arms all require comprehensive NGS + HERACLES-grade HER2 + DPYD/UGT1A1 documentation for screening.
guideline_status: NCCN Colon Cancer v1.2026 + ESMO mCRC (Cervantes 2023) + March 2024 FDA fluoropyrimidine label update + CPIC DPYD/UGT1A1: comprehensive NGS, HER2 IHC with HERACLES reflex FISH, MMR IHC orthogonal to NGS-MSI, and DPYD genotyping are guideline-endorsed pre-decision steps in any 1L mCRC patient. Signatera carries Medicare coverage in stage II-IV CRC.
rationale_summary: All five personas converged on the workup gates without dissent. The single FoundationOne CDx (or equivalent) send-out returns KRAS A59T VAF + clonality, full extended RAS, BRAF V600, ERBB2 amplification, PIK3CA M1043I somatic call, TP53 R273 substitution (R273H vs C vs L vs S), SMAD4 R361H, and the 20q segment boundaries; HERACLES-graded HER2 IHC/FISH is the single most-actionable target check not yet done on the case (T-DXd ORR ~38% in DESTINY-CRC02 if positive); MMR IHC orthogonal to NGS-MSI closes the ICI door definitively rather than presumptively; DPYD + UGT1A1 are mandated by the March 2024 FDA fluoropyrimidine label update and the 2026 NCCN colon guideline; Signatera baseline before CRS-HIPEC gives the lead-time signal for peritoneal recurrence after surgery. The workup unblocks the rest of the ranking and lets the team make biomarker-conditional decisions on real values rather than presumed ones.
open_questions: Whether the comprehensive panel run at the patient's home institution covered POLE/POLD1 proofreading-domain variants (early-onset 37yo bracket; if not, focused add-on warranted).
Whether tissue is sufficient for the Signatera tumor-informed bespoke build (16-variant WES design) without a second FFPE pull.
likelihood_of_effect: High — diagnostic certainty across seven decision gates; not a therapeutic but the precondition for every therapeutic call below.
toxicity_burden: Low (none — diagnostic test on archival tissue + peripheral blood draw)

counter_productive_moa.description: Diagnostic workup; no mechanism-level risk to a therapeutic goal.

overall: **Unblocks anti-EGFR eligibility, HER2-directed options, ICI doors, PIK3CA confirmation, fluoropyrimidine safety, and post-CRS surveillance from a single archival-block send-out plus blood draws.**

intervention_label: Continue FOLFIRI + bevacizumab through the peri-operative window (bev hold 4-6 weeks pre-CRS and 4-6 weeks post-CRS); discuss FOLFOXIRI + bev intensification per TRIBE/TRIBE2 if oxaliplatin-naive and ECOG 1 confirmed
expected_benefit: FOLFIRI + bev: AVF2107g mOS 20.3 vs 15.6 mo (HR 0.66, p<0.001); BICC-C confirmed FOLFIRI as the favored irinotecan backbone (mOS 23.1 mo); MAVERICC supports FOLFIRI-bev = FOLFOX-bev in 1L. FOLFOXIRI + bev intensification: TRIBE mPFS 12.1 vs 9.7 mo (HR 0.75); TRIBE2 mOS 27.4 vs 22.5 mo (HR 0.82) — ESMO MCBS 3 in a fit young patient with peritoneal-predominant disease.
key_risks: FOLFIRI: G3+ neutropenia ~25%, G3+ diarrhea ~14%; bev wound-healing / bowel-perforation risk → 4-6 week peri-op hold is the binding safety constraint, not optional.
FOLFOXIRI intensification adds cumulative oxaliplatin neuropathy (rate-limiting for a 37yo with a long runway — bake OPTIMOX stop-and-go in if pursued).
Without DPYD + UGT1A1 results (rank-1 workup), the FOLFIRI dose calibration is operating blind on the *2A / HapB3 / *28 carriers most at risk of late cumulative toxicity.
preference_alignment: Matches 'surface the full option space' (SoC backbone explicitly named); matches efficacy-leaning 0.7 (FOLFOXIRI intensification is on the table for ECOG 1, age 37); trial-prefer satisfied by CAIRO6 (NCT02758951) as the perioperative-chemo + CRS-HIPEC template even though new enrollment is closed.
guideline_status: NCCN Colon Cancer v1.2026 category 1 for FOLFIRI + bev 1L; category 2A preferred for FOLFOXIRI + bev 1L in fit patients; ESMO mCRC Cervantes 2023 level I, recommendation A.
rationale_summary: Universal endorsement on the SoC floor. The conservative seat anchored this at rank 1 of its own list and the concensusite seat raised the FOLFOXIRI intensification conversation that the critic and risktaker also flagged. The non-negotiable thread is the bevacizumab peri-op hold (4-6 weeks each side of CRS, documented wound closure before resumption) — skipping it is the single highest-yield way to harm the patient before any KRAS or PIK3CA question matters. Whether to intensify to FOLFOXIRI + bev is a young-patient / fit-patient conversation supported by TRIBE / TRIBE2 OS data and ESMO recommendation A; the right framing is permitted preferred upgrade rather than mandatory switch from the FOLFIRI the patient is tolerating. Pharmacogenomics (DPYD + UGT1A1) must land before any dose escalation.
open_questions: Whether the treating team prefers FOLFIRI continuation or TRIBE-style FOLFOXIRI + bev intensification before the CRS-HIPEC window — both are guideline-supported.
Optimal washout between the last FOLFIRI dose and CRS to limit perioperative neutropenia (typical 3-4 weeks).
likelihood_of_effect: High — replicated phase 3 OS signal across AVF2107g, BICC-C, MAVERICC, TRIBE2; ESMO MCBS 3.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (G3+ neutropenia ~25-30%, G3+ diarrhea ~14% on FOLFIRI; cumulative neuropathy and bev wound-healing constraints with intensification)

counter_productive_moa.description: Bevacizumab wound-healing impairment in the peri-operative window — managed by the 4-6 week hold; not a mechanism-level blunting of the cytotoxic backbone.

overall: **The replicated 1L OS backbone with the longest safety dossier in the case; the bev peri-op hold is the load-bearing safety thread, and FOLFOXIRI intensification is a permitted upgrade for a fit 37-year-old.**

intervention_label: Low-dose aspirin 160 mg PO QD as PIK3CA-pathway-altered adjunct (ALASCCA-derived), held 5-7 days pre-CRS and resumed post-op once surgical hemostasis allows
expected_benefit: ALASCCA (Frödin / Martling 2025 NEJM, n=626) in PIK3CA exon 9/20 Group A: 3-yr time-to-recurrence HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.24-0.98, p=0.044); Group B (other PI3K-pathway alterations) HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.21-0.83, p=0.013). Liao 2012 NHS/HPFS (n=964): HR 0.18 (95% CI 0.06-0.61) CRC-specific mortality in PIK3CA-mutant patients. Yang/Meyerhardt 2024 CALGB/SWOG 80702 celecoxib PIK3CA-activating subset: DFS HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.35-0.88); OS HR 0.41 (95% CI 0.21-0.79). M1043I is exon 20 kinase-domain → Group A.
key_risks: G3+ GI bleeding ~3% on ALASCCA aspirin arm vs ~2% placebo; baseline GI history and PPI consideration recommended.
Peri-operative aspirin hold (5-7 days pre-CRS, resume post-op once hemostasis allows) needs explicit handoff to the surgical team.
Compounded bleeding risk with bevacizumab co-administration is real but well-mapped; coordinate hold timing with the bev cycle.
preference_alignment: Trivial cost (~$0.05/pill), OTC, no veto applies. Matches the 'surface the full option space' framing as a cheap layered adjunct rather than competing with systemic therapy for the lead slot.
guideline_status: NCCN Colon Cancer v4.2025 formally adopted the ALASCCA recommendation: consider PIK3CA testing in stage II-III colon cancer and offer low-dose aspirin 100-162 mg PO daily for 3 years in PIK3CA-mutated patients. The metastatic-setting extrapolation is honest — ALASCCA enrolled resected stage I-III; post-CRS-HIPEC the disease state is adjuvant-equivalent and the class safety profile transfers cleanly.
rationale_summary: All five personas surfaced this. The critic ranked it #1 on RoB2 grounds — the only phase 3 RCT in the dossier with a biomarker match and a primary endpoint that crossed alpha — and the concensusite carried it with the NCCN v4.2025 adoption flag. Three independent biomarker-stratified datasets aligned directionally on the COX-2 / PGE2 / PI3K mechanism (ALASCCA RCT, 80702 celecoxib subgroup, Liao 2012 observational). The honest qualifier the entire board co-signed: ALASCCA enrolled resected adjuvant patients, not stage IV with active peritoneal disease; the mechanism rationale carries cleanly to the post-CRS adjuvant-equivalent state but the metastatic-setting efficacy claim is extrapolation rather than endpoint-validated. Position it as a layered adjunct on top of whichever systemic backbone the team runs, not as a replacement for any of them.
open_questions: Whether the M1043I-specific subset within ALASCCA Group A behaves the same as the canonical H1047R/E545K/E542K hotspots — unreported at that resolution.
Optimal duration in the metastatic-equivalent state — ALASCCA used 3 years adjuvant; the post-HIPEC analog is judgment-grade.
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate — three concordant biomarker-stratified signals (ALASCCA HR 0.49, 80702 celecoxib OS HR 0.41, Liao 2012 HR 0.18) but indication gap from resected adjuvant to metastatic-equivalent post-HIPEC.
toxicity_burden: Low (G3+ GI bleed ~3% vs 2% on ALASCCA; manageable with PPI + perioperative hold)

counter_productive_moa.description: Aspirin hold required around bev cycles and CRS-HIPEC to avoid additive bleeding; mechanism direction itself is supportive, not counter-productive.

overall: **The only RoB2:Low phase 3 RCT in the dossier with a biomarker match — a cheap, layered, guideline-adopted adjunct that almost any other pick stacks on top of.**

intervention_label: Cytoreductive surgery at a high-volume peritoneal-surface-malignancy center; if HIPEC is performed, mitomycin C HIPEC rather than oxaliplatin HIPEC, with PRODIGE 7 framing in the consent conversation
expected_benefit: CRS retains the survival spine in CRC peritoneal metastases (NCCN-endorsed mOS 30-40 mo range for selected patients at experienced centers, PCI < 20). PRODIGE 7 (Quenet 2021 Lancet Oncol, n=265): adding oxaliplatin HIPEC to CRS did NOT improve OS (41.7 vs 41.2 mo, HR ~1.00) or RFS (13.1 vs 11.1 mo) and increased 60-day morbidity. Mitomycin C HIPEC keeps the pharmacokinetic peritoneal:plasma AUC advantage (Van der Speeten ~20-25x for hydrophilic drug delivery) and was not the agent PRODIGE 7 eliminated. CAIRO6 (Rovers 2024) supports the perioperative-chemo + CRS-HIPEC structure for PFS even where OS is unchanged.
key_risks: 60-day morbidity higher in HIPEC arms; surgeon volume / center experience drives morbidity more than perfusate choice.
Oxaliplatin HIPEC for CRC is essentially closed by PRODIGE 7 — mitomycin C is the lower-bad choice if HIPEC is performed at all.
Post-CRS recovery delays systemic therapy by 4-8 weeks; bracket with ctDNA baseline pre-op + day-30-60 post-op draw.
preference_alignment: Matches the user's explicit free-text framing 'treat the planned CRS-HIPEC window as a sequencing constraint' rather than vetoing the surgical plan; honors patient autonomy with the treating surgical team.
guideline_status: NCCN Colon Cancer v1.2026 endorses CRS at category 2A for selected patients with limited resectable peritoneal disease at experienced centers; HIPEC language is deliberately permissive — may be considered at selected centers — because PRODIGE 7 is negative for the oxaliplatin agent. ESMO mCRC carries the same caveat.
rationale_summary: Four of five personas converged: CRS retains the OS signal, oxaliplatin HIPEC does not (PRODIGE 7), and mitomycin C HIPEC at a high-volume center (>20 cases/yr; major US Sugarbaker-trained programs include MSK, MD Anderson, Mayo, City of Hope, Wake Forest, UPMC, Cleveland Clinic, Moffitt) is the defensible compromise if the surgical team and patient elect HIPEC. The critic's dissent is honest and load-bearing: the strict-evidence read is that no randomized OS signal exists for mitomycin C HIPEC either, and the negative trifecta (PRODIGE 7 + COLOPEC + PROPHYLOCHIP) closes the OS claim for HIPEC as a class. The risktaker's qualifier kept Van der Speeten's MMC pharmacokinetic argument on the table as the mechanism PRODIGE 7 did not test. The framing the family needs to hear: CRS = OS-validated; HIPEC ≠ OS-validated; mitomycin > oxaliplatin if HIPEC is on the table. NCT04779554 (Kentucky / Vermont mitomycin C dosing trial) and NCT04861558 (EFFIPEC CRS vs CRS+HIPEC, Sweden/India — not US-accessible) are the trial routes.
open_questions: Whether the surgical team's preferred center handles ≥20 CRS-HIPEC cases/yr (the load-bearing predictor of 60-day morbidity).
Whether the team accepts the Yale MRT-guided HIPEC selection feasibility trial (NCT07291180) to personalize agent choice.
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate for CRS (NCCN-endorsed selected-patient mOS 30-40 mo); Low for the HIPEC component specifically (PRODIGE 7 negative for oxaliplatin; no positive randomized signal for mitomycin C).
toxicity_burden: High (CRS-HIPEC 60-day morbidity ~25-40% G3+; bleeding, anastomotic leak, infection, prolonged ileus; treatment-related mortality 1-3% at high-volume centers, higher at lower-volume)

counter_productive_moa.description: Critic dissent stands on mechanism grounds: oxaliplatin HIPEC negative randomized OS readout; mitomycin C HIPEC has no positive randomized OS readout either — the procedure window itself delays systemic therapy.

overall: **CRS retains the OS spine for resectable peritoneal CRC; HIPEC sits outside randomized OS validation — mitomycin C is the defensible perfusate at a high-volume center if HIPEC is elected.**

intervention_label: Inavolisib 9 mg PO QD + bevacizumab on INTRINSIC (NCT04929223) PIK3CA-mutant arm — enroll at progression past FOLFIRI-bev or post-CRS-HIPEC, contingent on M1043I somatic + clonal confirmation from the rank-1 NGS
expected_benefit: INAVO120 (Jhaveri 2024 NEJM, n=325) in HR+/HER2- PIK3CA-mutant breast: PFS HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.32-0.59), mPFS 15.0 vs 7.3 mo — RoB2:Low cross-tumor pharmacology anchor that drove the Oct 2024 FDA approval. CRC fallback is Juric 2018 alpelisib phase 1a: 2 PRs in the n=134 CRC subset of a PI3K-altered solid-tumor basket. INTRINSIC PIK3CA-mut mCRC arm-specific PFS / OS not yet published. Vasan 2019 tagged M1043 as a kinase-domain activating allele sensitizing to PI3K-alpha-selective inhibition.
key_risks: Hyperglycemia (any-grade 58.6%, G3+ 5.6% on INAVO120) — fasting glucose + HbA1c baseline; preemptive metformin / SGLT2-inhibitor plan if HbA1c ≥7%.
G3+ stomatitis 5.6%, G3+ diarrhea 3.7%, treatment discontinuation 6.5% in INAVO120.
KRAS A59T co-activation may blunt single-pathway PI3K-alpha response — the realistic upside is depth-of-response augmentation and PFS extension, not single-agent home-run.
preference_alignment: Matches efficacy-leaning 0.7 + trial-prefer + 'surface all options'; off-label outside the trial has no compendium support and no payer access, so INTRINSIC is the cleanest route (Genentech covers the drug under protocol).
guideline_status: On-label only in HR+/HER2- breast (Itovebi, FDA Oct 2024). Not in NCCN Colon v1.2026. INTRINSIC trial enrollment is the guideline-permitted route for biomarker-defined off-label PIK3CA-axis options in mCRC.
rationale_summary: Mixed-grade endorsement under documented dissent — exactly the case where Hard Rule 3 applies. The advocate ranked inavolisib #1 (mechanism-matched PIK3CA M1043I; bev continuation tracks the patient's current regimen); the risktaker ranked #2 with confidence-low; the conservative reserved for 2L on cross-tumor evidence grounds; the critic placed at rank 3 with explicit dissent on cross-tumor extrapolation (INAVO120 is breast, not CRC; INTRINSIC arm-specific CRC data not posted; CRC fallback is 2 PRs in Juric 2018 phase 1a); the concensusite dissented on guideline-fit (1L displacement of category-1 chemo+bev backbone is outside NCCN endorsement). Synthesis: position as INTRINSIC trial enrollment at progression past FOLFIRI-bev or post-CRS-HIPEC, not 1L displacement; M1043I somatic + clonal confirmation from the rank-1 NGS is the gating step the advocate, conservative, and critic all named; the cross-tumor evidence caveat carries forward in the consent conversation. The trial slot is real and the mechanism match is the cleanest in the dossier; the off-label use case is not.
open_questions: Whether INTRINSIC will accept M1043I as kinase-domain-activating without a sponsor exception (canonical hotspots H1047R/E545K/E542K dominate the registry).
Whether INTRINSIC has a KRAS-A59T-eligible RAS arm slot in parallel — sponsor confirmation (global-roche-genentech-trials@gene.com, 888-662-6728).
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate ASSUMING M1043I confirmed somatic + clonal — INAVO120 PFS HR 0.43 is cross-tumor breast; CRC efficacy is hypothesis-grade (Juric 2018 2 PRs / 134 CRC subset; INTRINSIC arm-specific PFS unpublished).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (G3+ hyperglycemia 5.6%, any-grade 58.6%; G3+ stomatitis 5.6%; G3+ diarrhea 3.7%; discontinuation 6.5%)

counter_productive_moa.description: Critic and concensusite dissented on mechanism grounds: KRAS A59T co-activation may blunt single-pathway PI3K-alpha inhibition; cross-tumor breast extrapolation does not address CRC's downstream-RAS escape biology.

overall: **The cleanest PIK3CA M1043I mechanism match in the dossier, gated by cross-tumor extrapolation and KRAS A59T co-activation — trial-route only, sequenced at progression rather than 1L displacement.**

intervention_label: Botensilimab + balstilimab at 2L+/3L+ after FOLFIRI-bev progression — operational paths: USC NCT06336902 (BOT/BAL + fasting-mimicking diet + IV vitamin C in KRAS-mutant MSS mCRC) is most actionable; Agenus EAP (NCT06751524) once standard lines exhausted; CCTG BATTMAN NCT07152821 is the registrational readout pending
expected_benefit: Bullock 2024 Nat Med phase 1b (n=101) in refractory MSS mCRC: all-comer ORR 17% (95% CI 10-26); no-liver-metastases (NLM) subset ORR 22% with mOS 20.9 mo; active-liver-mets subset ORR 5%. Randomized phase 2 update (Bullock 2024 ASCO GI / ESMO GI, n=123 NLM): BOT+BAL ORR 19% with mOS approaching 21 mo, peritoneal-site responses specifically called out. Patient's phenotype (liver mets resected, peritoneal-dominant active disease) maps onto the NLM responder subset.
key_risks: G3+ irAE 35-38% across phase 1 and phase 2 update; G3+ colitis 12%, G3+ hepatitis 8%; pyrexia 38% any-grade; treatment-related deaths 0 in dossier.
Selection bias on NLM phenotype: post-hoc-defined subgroup in the Bullock expansion, not pre-specified primary stratum.
If recurrence appears at the liver after CRS, response probability drops to the 5% LM-subset rate — the peritoneal-only window may not persist.
FMD + IV vitamin C layer in NCT06336902 is hypothesis-only with no controlled signal; conservative dissent flagged stacking research-only adjuncts on ICI in active peritoneal disease.
preference_alignment: Matches efficacy-leaning 0.7 + trial-prefer + 'surface all options'; USC NCT06336902 explicitly enrolls KRAS-mutant MSS mCRC so A59T is structurally in; access path is southern California sites (~15 patients) requiring travel.
guideline_status: Not in NCCN. CCTG BATTMAN (NCT07152821) vs BSC is the registrational confirmation; reads out 2027-2028. Agenus Expanded Access Protocol (NCT06751524) is FDA-authorized for treating-physician-initiated requests in chemo-refractory patients across multiple cancers including CRC.
rationale_summary: All five personas named bot/bal as the most decision-relevant MSS-CRC immunotherapy signal in the modern era, and the NLM phenotype match for this patient is unusually clean. The conservative seat ranked it #4 with reserve-for-3L+ posture (sequencing past 2L documented chemo-refractory status); the critic ranked #2 with explicit dissent on single-arm phase 1b plus randomized-vs-monotherapy phase 2 grounds (no BSC comparator); the risktaker / advocate ranked top-3 in the post-1L slot. Synthesis: position as the post-1L pivot once FOLFIRI-bev has progressed and the peritoneal-only phenotype persists; USC NCT06336902 is the most operationally actionable today (Charlean Ketchens, Charlean.Ketchens@med.usc.edu, 323-865-0451); EAP via med.info@agenusbio.com / 781-202-1614 once 2L exhausted; BATTMAN OS readout pending. The G3+ colitis 12% and hepatitis 8% are the binding safety threads — baseline thyroid / hepatic / endocrine panel and a defined irAE-management algorithm per SITC/ASCO/NCCN are mandatory before initiation, especially in a patient recovering from CRS.
open_questions: Whether the patient is willing / able to travel to the USC site for NCT06336902 (southern California).
Whether the peritoneal-only phenotype persists after CRS-HIPEC (post-CRS imaging + Signatera kinetic).
Whether the FMD + IV vitamin C adjuncts in NCT06336902 are protocol-mandatory or modifiable.
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate in the NLM peritoneal-dominant subset (ORR 22%, mOS 20.9 mo Bullock 2024) — strongest MSS-CRC ICI signal of the decade but selection bias + no BSC comparator until BATTMAN reads out.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (G3+ colitis 12%, G3+ hepatitis 8%, G3+ pyrexia in subset; cumulative G3+ irAE 35-38%)

counter_productive_moa.description: Critic dissented on evidence-quality mechanism (post-hoc NLM subgroup); conservative dissented on stacking research-only FMD + IV-C adjuncts on Fc-enhanced anti-CTLA-4 in active peritoneal disease.

overall: **Strongest modern MSS-CRC immunotherapy signal mapped to the patient's NLM peritoneal phenotype; 2L+ trial-route only, gated by FOLFIRI-bev progression and travel logistics.**

intervention_label: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) 5.4 mg/kg IV Q3W on the DESTINY-CRC02 pathway — CONDITIONAL on HER2 IHC 3+ or ISH ratio ≥2.0 returning positive from the rank-1 workup; RAS-mutant-allowed per the 2024 pan-tumor accelerated approval
expected_benefit: DESTINY-CRC02 (Raghav 2024): T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg ORR ~38% in HER2-positive mCRC including RAS-mutant patients (the MOUNTAINEER tucatinib + trastuzumab label excludes RAS-mutant, but T-DXd does not). Pan-tumor accelerated approval (April 2024) removed the RAS-WT restriction. HER2 amplification covers another 3-5% of mCRC and is the single most-actionable target check not yet done in this case. The dual TOP1-payload rationale aligns with the patient's 20q11 TOP1 co-amplification on existing NGS.
key_risks: G3+ ILD / pneumonitis 5-10% across DESTINY trials; baseline + Q3W chest imaging surveillance; treatment-related ILD deaths reported.
G3+ neutropenia ~30%, G3+ nausea/vomiting 10-15%, G3+ fatigue 10%.
RAS-mutant subset within DESTINY-CRC02 carries lower absolute response (mid-30% range vs RAS-WT) — A59T-specific data are not reported.
preference_alignment: Matches the user's free-text 'surface the full option space' and efficacy-leaning 0.7; the conditional HER2-positive branch is the wildcard upside Bullock-class ICI signal cannot match if the test returns positive.
guideline_status: FDA pan-tumor accelerated approval April 2024 for HER2-positive (IHC 3+) unresectable / metastatic solid tumors after prior systemic therapy. NCCN Colon v1.2026 supports T-DXd off-label in HER2-positive mCRC. HERACLES IHC 3+ in >50% of cells or IHC 2+ with FISH ratio ≥2.0 (pmid:27108243) is the historically defensible call.
rationale_summary: Universal endorsement contingent on the rank-1 workup. The risktaker named T-DXd as the wildcard upside if HER2 amp returns positive; the concensusite called out that the T-DXd pan-tumor approval is RAS-mutant-allowed (DESTINY-CRC02 specifically enrolled RAS-mutant patients), distinct from MOUNTAINEER which the RAS-WT label excludes for this patient. The conservative seat agreed HER2 status is the binding pre-2L decision that cannot be locked until the comprehensive panel returns. The advocate framed T-DXd as the cleanest HER2-pathway option for an A59T patient if HER2 IHC 3+ confirms. No persona dissented. The intervention is biomarker-conditional — if HER2 returns negative (most likely; 3-5% prior probability), this rec is foreclosed. If positive, it moves to the front of the post-1L slot conversation alongside bot/bal, and ranks 5 (inavolisib) and 6 (bot/bal) get re-prioritized against it.
open_questions: HERACLES IHC + reflex FISH result from the rank-1 workup.
Whether the patient would prioritize a HER2-positive T-DXd trial slot (NCT04744831) over the standard 2L FOLFOX-bev backbone if both became available.
ILD monitoring infrastructure at the treating center (baseline PFTs + chest CT + Q3W surveillance).
likelihood_of_effect: High in HER2 IHC 3+ subset (DESTINY-CRC02 ORR ~38% including RAS-mutant); contingent on HER2 status — foreclosed if HER2 negative (3-5% prior probability of positive).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (G3+ neutropenia ~30%, G3+ ILD 5-10% with treatment-related deaths reported, G3+ nausea/vomiting 10-15%)

counter_productive_moa.description: On-target ILD is the dominant counter-productive vector; RAS-mutant subset has lower absolute response than RAS-WT but A59T-specific behavior unreported.

overall: **The single most-actionable wildcard if HER2 amplification returns positive — RAS-mutant-allowed under the 2024 pan-tumor accelerated approval, and the cleanest HER2 path for an A59T patient.**

intervention_label: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) on RASolve-GI (NCT06445062) — GATED on Revolution Medicines confirming KRAS A59T eligibility; JAB-23E73 (NCT06973564, Jacobio, KRAS-alteration-agnostic by public text) as the fallback inquiry; S241656 (NCT05786924, Servier ERK inhibitor, codon-agnostic) as the secondary fallback
expected_benefit: RMC-6236 is the first pan-RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor with documented regression across G12/G13/Q61 PDXs at 25-50 mg/kg (Knox/Jiang Nature 2024). A59T sits in switch-II in a way that preserves the binding interface, so mechanism plausibly carries. RASolve-GI (NCT06445062) protocol text reads 'RAS-mutated CRC' without an explicit codon gate; sponsor-level operational definition usually narrows to codons 12/13/61. JAB-23E73 reads codon-agnostic and excludes prior KRAS-inhibitor exposure (the patient has none). S241656 lists KRAS/HRAS/NRAS/BRAF/CRAF alterations without codon restriction. ZERO published A59T-specific clinical efficacy in any program.
key_risks: Sponsor may rule A59T ineligible — the pick collapses entirely if RevMed says no.
Class-typical RAS(ON) toxicity: rash (acneiform 30-40% any-grade), GI (nausea / diarrhea), hepatic — manageable but real; cumulative AE profile in CRC still maturing.
Mechanism plausibility is not evidence — the critic's veto rests on n=0 A59T efficacy + protocol-defined codon exclusion on the flagship monotherapy basket NCT05379985.
Pause around CRS-HIPEC will eat into the PFS clock.
preference_alignment: Matches efficacy-leaning 0.7 + 'surface all options' + trial-prefer; this is the asymmetric-upside single phone call (medinfo@revmed.com / 1-844-2-REVMED) that the user's preference set explicitly authorizes surfacing. Conservative dissent rests on prudence rather than user preference.
guideline_status: Investigational. FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation 2024 for previously treated KRAS G12X PDAC; FDA Expanded Access Protocol May 2026 for PDAC only (not CRC). Not in NCCN. Trial-enrollment principle applies for atypical KRAS alleles.
rationale_summary: The dissent-and-veto thread is unresolved and must be surfaced rather than flattened. The advocate and risktaker ranked this top-2 on the asymmetric-upside argument — A59T is the single allele in the case dossier that the G12C-selective programs (sotorasib, adagrasib, divarasib) cannot touch, and RMC-6236 is the only active program with plausible mechanism reach. The conservative seat ranked #5 with explicit 'hypothetical until sponsor confirms' framing; the concensusite dissented on guideline-fit grounds (n=0 A59T clinical data; 1L displacement of the category-1 backbone is outside NCCN endorsement); the critic vetoed on evidence-quality grounds (mechanism plausibility ≠ evidence; flagship monotherapy basket NCT05379985 restricts to codons 12/13/61 by protocol text; the Knox/Jiang Nature papers are preclinical RAS(ON) pan-allele mechanism plausibility, not A59T-specific clinical readout). Hard Rule 1 override documented: keep the row in the table with status=considered_with_caveats so the user sees what was considered, with the critic's veto explicitly named and the load-bearing single phone call surfaced. The honest framing is that the single highest-yield action on the case is the medinfo@revmed.com / 1-844-2-REVMED call for A59T eligibility — if RevMed says yes, this becomes a real 2L+ contingent pick; if no, JAB-23E73 (sponsor: medical-affairs@jacobiopharma; Jacobio's atypical-KRAS-friendly arm) is the fallback inquiry, and S241656 ERK-inhibitor at Servier is the secondary fallback (codon-agnostic by protocol). If both fall through, this rec collapses.
open_questions: KRAS A59T eligibility on NCT06445062 — the single load-bearing inquiry (medinfo@revmed.com / 1-844-2-REVMED).
JAB-23E73 sponsor confirmation on A59T eligibility (Jacobio, NCT06973564) as the fallback.
Whether the patient is willing to travel for sponsor-confirmed enrollment (US + select EU/Australia sites for RASolve-GI).

toxicity_burden: Moderate (class-typical RAS(ON) acneiform rash 30-40% any-grade, GI nausea/diarrhea, hepatic; cumulative CRC profile maturing)

overall: **The asymmetric-upside single phone call for the atypical KRAS A59T allele — sponsor-confirmation-gated and critic-vetoed; document the inquiry result before any other RAS(ON) action.**

intervention_label: Post-CRS-HIPEC 2L+ bench: FOLFOX + bev (oxaliplatin-naive lane preserved) → aflibercept-FOLFIRI (VELOUR) or ramucirumab-FOLFIRI (RAISE) anti-angiogenic switch → SUNLIGHT TAS-102 + bev → FRESCO-2 fruquintinib → regorafenib (CORRECT / CONCUR)
expected_benefit: Sequential 2L+ backbone with replicated phase 3 OS signal at each line. NO16966 (FOLFOX/XELOX + bev) anchors the chemo + bev backbone mPFS 9.4 vs 8.0 mo (HR 0.83). VELOUR aflibercept-FOLFIRI mOS 13.5 vs 12.1 (HR 0.82). RAISE ramucirumab-FOLFIRI mOS 13.3 vs 11.7 (HR 0.84). SUNLIGHT TAS-102 + bev mOS 10.8 vs 7.5 (HR 0.61). FRESCO-2 fruquintinib mOS HR 0.66. CORRECT regorafenib HR 0.77; CONCUR HR 0.55. Stacked, the field reaches 28-32 mo mOS for fit patients.
key_risks: Cumulative oxaliplatin neuropathy is rate-limiting for a 37-year-old with a long runway — bake OPTIMOX stop-and-go in.
Anti-angiogenic continuation past 2L compounds wound-healing / bleeding / hypertension risk.
Anchored on replicated RCT data but no biomarker enrichment — this is the floor any feature-targeting pick has to beat, not the upside swing.
preference_alignment: Matches 'surface all options' (SoC bench explicitly named); efficacy-leaning 0.7 honored by sequencing through the highest-OS options at each line; oxaliplatin-naive status preserves the cleanest 2L drug for the moment it is needed.
guideline_status: NCCN Colon Cancer v1.2026 category 1 at each line (FOLFOX + bev 2L; aflibercept-FOLFIRI / ramucirumab-FOLFIRI 2L; TAS-102 + bev 3L; fruquintinib / regorafenib 3-4L). ESMO mCRC level I.
rationale_summary: Endorsed by the three guideline / evidence-anchored seats (conservative, critic, concensusite) as the proven sequencing backbone the experimental arms have to beat. Not Libby's targetable-feature scope strictly speaking — these regimens act on the patient's MSS / RAS-mutant / 1L-bev-tolerant phenotype rather than on a stated targetable feature — but the critic flagged in their notes that these are 'the interventions with replicated RCT evidence the patient should actually receive,' and surfacing them honors the user's 'surface the full option space' framing. Sequenced post-CRS-HIPEC, sequenced around the bev peri-op hold, and modulated by the rank-1 DPYD + UGT1A1 results. Ranked here rather than higher because Libby's primary deliverable is the feature-targeted ranking; this row is the SoC reference frame the other picks layer on or replace.
open_questions: Whether FOLFOX or FOLFOXIRI runs pre-CRS-HIPEC (rank 2) changes the 2L drug choice (FOLFOX-naive vs FOLFOX-exposed).
Whether ctDNA-driven adjuvant-duration decisions enter (NRG-GI008 CIRCULATE-US trial route per concensusite rank 5).
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate-High — replicated phase 3 OS signal at each line; stacked sequencing 28-32 mo mOS achievable in fit patients.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (cumulative oxaliplatin neuropathy is rate-limiting; G3+ neutropenia and diarrhea at each line; anti-angiogenic AE compound)

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanism-level counter-productive vector; cumulative neuropathy and anti-angiogenic compound AEs are patient-level toxicity, not therapeutic-goal blunting.

overall: **The replicated 2L+ phase 3 OS floor the experimental picks have to beat — bake OPTIMOX in for the long young-patient runway and modulate by DPYD/UGT1A1 results.**

intervention_label: Cetuximab or panitumumab — default AVOID at 1L per Sorich 2015 meta-analysis; ASCEND-CRC platform (NCT07318389) research-framework rechallenge defensible only at later lines if a specific A59T functional argument is made and the rank-1 NGS confirms full RAS / BRAF clearance
expected_benefit: Sorich 2015 meta-analysis (n=5,948 across 9 RCTs, RoB2:Low): OS HR 1.08 (95% CI 0.91-1.28) and PFS HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.78-1.36) in any-new-RAS-mutant subset — no benefit. Schirripa 2015 (n=786, retrospective): 0/9 responders among NRAS-mutant anti-EGFR-treated patients. Arena 2021 (n=169, ROBINS-I:Moderate): A59 / A146 / K117 alleles show 'occasional responders' with weaker MAPK signaling than canonical G12 mutants — hypothesis-generating only. Lochhead 2018: single-patient case report of -36% target-lesion change on panitumumab + FOLFIRI in a KRAS A59T tumor — anecdote-grade.
key_risks: Anti-EGFR-class acneiform rash (Grade 3+ 10-20%), hypomagnesemia, paronychia, infusion reactions.
Population-level meta-analytic data (n=5,948) say no benefit; treating the Lochhead n=1 case as practice-changing inverts the evidence pyramid.
Compounded wound-healing risk if administered around CRS-HIPEC.
preference_alignment: The advocate and risktaker argued the 'surface all options' framing authorizes outside-guideline thinking when biology supports it (Arena 2021 functional data); the conservative and concensusite seats vetoed at the population-evidence level. The synthesis splits the difference: default AVOID at 1L (population-level wins), research-framework defensible at later lines if a specific A59T functional argument is made (Arena 2021 framing not foreclosed).
guideline_status: NCCN Colon Cancer v1.2026 treats any non-WT RAS (KRAS or NRAS exons 2/3/4) as an anti-EGFR exclusion at the guideline level; KRAS A59T sits in exon 3. ESMO mCRC carries the same exclusion at level I.
rationale_summary: Universal documented veto / dissent at 1L, with a structured research-framework path at later lines surfaced explicitly so the user sees what was considered and rejected. The concensusite and conservative seats vetoed on guideline-fit and population-evidence grounds (Sorich 2015 n=5,948 RoB2:Low meta-analytic OS HR 1.08; current NCCN / ESMO consensus is that A59T is RAS-mutant for anti-EGFR purposes). The advocate and risktaker dissented on the population-level closure: Arena 2021 functionally characterized A59-class alleles as retaining partial residual EGFR pathway sensitivity in some cases, and the conservative seat itself softened on cross-critique to 'default AVOID pending functional characterization, with anti-EGFR rechallenge under a research framework (ASCEND-CRC NCT07318389) defensible at later lines if a specific A59T functional argument is made.' Synthesis: row carried as considered_with_caveats per Hard Rule 1; default AVOID at 1L; not welded shut for later lines. The Lochhead 2018 single-patient PR is acknowledged as anecdotal, not practice-changing.
open_questions: Whether ASCEND-CRC NCT07318389 will accept an A59T patient at later lines under a research framework with a documented A59T-specific functional argument.
Whether the rank-1 NGS confirms full extended-RAS clearance and BRAF V600 wild-type (the secondary anti-EGFR eligibility gates beyond KRAS itself).
likelihood_of_effect: Low at 1L (Sorich 2015 OS HR 1.08 in any-new-RAS-mutant n=5,948); uncharacterized at later lines under a research framework with A59T-specific functional argument.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (G3+ acneiform rash 10-20%, hypomagnesemia, paronychia; manageable but real)

counter_productive_moa.description: Conservative + concensusite veto stands on mechanism: A59T is treated as RAS-activating by NCCN consensus, so anti-EGFR is mechanism-counter-productive at the population level.

overall: **Default AVOID at 1L per population-level meta-analysis; structured research-framework rechallenge defensible at later lines on Arena 2021 functional grounds — not welded shut, not 1L-recommendable.**

intervention_label: Sotorasib (CodeBreaK 300) + panitumumab and adagrasib (KRYSTAL-1) + cetuximab — NOT RECOMMENDED for KRAS A59T (allele-incompatible)
expected_benefit: None for KRAS A59T. Sotorasib and adagrasib are covalent G12C-selective inhibitors that exploit the switch-II cysteine present in G12C tumors; KRAS A59T has alanine-to-threonine at codon 59 (switch-II) with NO cysteine to covalently target. CodeBreaK 300 and KRYSTAL-1 enrolled G12C-only.
key_risks: N/A — mechanism-incompatible; would expose the patient to class toxicity (rash, GI, hepatic) with zero target engagement.
preference_alignment: Universal board veto; no preference rationale lifts the mechanism mismatch.
guideline_status: FDA approval for sotorasib + panitumumab and adagrasib + cetuximab is KRAS G12C-restricted; NCCN Colon v1.2026 treats them as G12C-only.
rationale_summary: Universal veto across all five personas — the only intervention in the case where all five board members independently named the mechanism mismatch (switch-II cysteine absent at A59 → no covalent handle). Carried in the table per Hard Rule 1 so the user sees what was considered and rejected explicitly, with the allele-incompatibility documented. This row exists to close the door on a question that will keep coming up because the headlines around sotorasib + panitumumab in KRAS G12C mCRC are loud.
likelihood_of_effect: None — mechanism-incompatible at the covalent-warhead level; A59T lacks the switch-II cysteine the drugs target.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (class acneiform rash, GI nausea/diarrhea, hepatic) — but zero efficacy for A59T makes any AE counter-productive by definition.

counter_productive_moa.description: Universal veto on mechanism grounds: drug binds G12C-specific cysteine; A59T lacks the warhead substrate entirely.

overall: **Allele-incompatible — listed so the consultation team sees the closed door explicitly; the G12C-selective drugs cannot reach A59T at the covalent-warhead level.**

intervention_label: Single-agent pembrolizumab, dostarlimab, nivolumab, or nivolumab + ipilimumab — NOT RECOMMENDED in MSS / TMB-low / PD-L1-negative mCRC
expected_benefit: None for MSS / TMB-low / PD-L1-negative. Le 2015 NEJM defined the MMR-deficient / MSI-H ICI selectivity; CheckMate 142 anchors nivo-ipi in MSI-H. The pembrolizumab tumor-agnostic TMB-H label requires ≥10 mut/Mb on F1CDx (rank-1 workup will lock the number, but the intake reports TMB-low). PD-L1 is negative on file.
key_risks: N/A — phenotype-incompatible; would expose the patient to G3+ irAE without target-engaged benefit.
preference_alignment: Universal board veto; phenotype foreclosure (MSS + TMB-low + PD-L1-neg) is unambiguous.
guideline_status: NCCN Colon Cancer v1.2026 restricts pembrolizumab and dostarlimab to dMMR / MSI-H mCRC; tumor-agnostic TMB-H pembrolizumab label requires ≥10 mut/Mb on F1CDx.
rationale_summary: Universal veto across all five personas. Listed for the same Hard Rule 1 reason as the G12C row — closes a question that the family or referring team may ask about. The phenotype foreclosure is unambiguous: MSS by NGS, TMB-low by intake, PD-L1-negative by IHC, and the rank-1 MMR IHC orthogonal will close the door definitively (a 5% discordance call to MSI-H would reverse this entirely, which is why the workup row matters). If MMR IHC unexpectedly returns dMMR, single-agent pembrolizumab leaps to first-line consideration; until then, it is foreclosed.
open_questions: Whether the rank-1 MMR IHC orthogonal returns concordant MSS (~95% probability) or discordant MSI-H (~5%). Discordant MSI-H reverses this row entirely.
likelihood_of_effect: None — phenotype-incompatible (MSS / TMB-low / PD-L1-neg); unless rank-1 MMR IHC unexpectedly returns dMMR.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (G3+ irAE colitis, hepatitis, pneumonitis, endocrinopathy) — counter-productive without target engagement.

counter_productive_moa.description: Universal veto on phenotype grounds: ICI biology requires MSI-H or TMB-H or PD-L1-high substrate, none of which the patient presents.

overall: **Phenotype-foreclosed in MSS / TMB-low / PD-L1-negative — listed so the door is explicitly closed; the rank-1 MMR IHC orthogonal is the only path that reopens it.**

intervention_label: Eprenetapopt (APR-246) and rezatapopt (PC14586) for TP53 R273 — NOT RECOMMENDED (eprenetapopt solid-tumor program closed; rezatapopt is Y220C-only by design)
expected_benefit: None for TP53 R273. Eprenetapopt Aprea solid-tumor program effectively closed after Park 2022 phase 1b solid-tumor combination posted ORR 8% (2 PRs / 24 evaluable) with mPFS 1.7 mo; R273 subset not separately analyzed. Rezatapopt (PC14586, PYNNACLE NCT04585750) is structurally Y220C-binding-pocket-restricted by design and additionally requires KRAS wild-type — the patient is KRAS A59T mutated.
key_risks: N/A — neither drug is mechanistically accessible to the patient's allele / phenotype combination.
preference_alignment: Universal board veto; mechanism + program-status foreclosure.
guideline_status: Not in NCCN. PYNNACLE protocol restricts to TP53 Y220C + KRAS wild-type; eprenetapopt solid-tumor development discontinued post-2022.
rationale_summary: Universal veto across all five personas. Two distinct reasons foreclose the row: (1) eprenetapopt's solid-tumor program effectively wound down after Park 2022 posted 2 PRs / 24 evaluable with mPFS 1.7 mo and Aprea pivoted away; (2) rezatapopt is Y220C-binding-pocket-restricted by structural design (the drug was crystal-engineered for the Y220C cavity, not the R273 DNA-contact surface) and PYNNACLE additionally requires KRAS wild-type which A59T fails. Carried as a Hard Rule 1 'considered and rejected' row so the user sees the TP53 R273 reactivator question was raised and closed. Future ATR / WEE1 / HSP90 synthetic-lethal-with-mutant-p53 trial rationale remains a watch-list item for recurrence; the rank-1 NGS R273H-vs-C-vs-L-vs-S substitution call sharpens that conversation.
open_questions: Whether the rank-1 NGS report calls the specific R273 substitution (R273H, R273C, R273L, R273S, R273P) — sharpens any future synthetic-lethal trial discussion even though no current drug is accessible.
likelihood_of_effect: None — eprenetapopt solid-tumor program closed; rezatapopt is Y220C-restricted and KRAS-WT-only.
toxicity_burden: Low (none — drugs not accessible to this patient)

counter_productive_moa.description: Universal veto on program-status + structural-design grounds: drug-allele mismatch at the binding-pocket level.

overall: **Closed at the program + structural-design level; documented so the TP53 R273 reactivator question is explicitly addressed and the future ATR/WEE1 watch-list framing is preserved.**

intervention_label: Oxaliplatin HIPEC framed as OS-positive — NOT RECOMMENDED per PRODIGE 7 (negative OS at HR ~1.00) reinforced by COLOPEC and PROPHYLOCHIP
expected_benefit: None over CRS alone. PRODIGE 7 (Quenet 2021 Lancet Oncol, n=265, RoB2:Low): oxaliplatin HIPEC vs no HIPEC after CRS — OS 41.7 vs 41.2 mo (HR ~1.00), RFS 13.1 vs 11.1 mo, higher 60-day morbidity in the HIPEC arm. COLOPEC (Klaver 2019, adjuvant HIPEC for T4 / perforated) 18-mo peritoneal DFS 80.9 vs 76.2%, not significant. PROPHYLOCHIP-PRODIGE 15 (Goere 2020) second-look surgery + HIPEC 3-yr DFS 44 vs 53%, HR 0.97, p=0.82.
key_risks: Adds 60-day morbidity without OS benefit; treatment-related morbidity 25-40% G3+ across HIPEC arms in the negative trifecta.
preference_alignment: Universal board veto except the risktaker's qualified position (MMC HIPEC > oxaliplatin HIPEC at high-volume centers, but neither randomized-OS-positive); honors the user's 'surface options honestly' framing by stating the negative randomized result plainly.
guideline_status: NCCN Colon Cancer v1.2026 deliberately permissive on HIPEC; oxaliplatin HIPEC specifically is essentially closed for CRC after PRODIGE 7.
rationale_summary: Four-of-five veto on framing oxaliplatin HIPEC as OS-positive. The risktaker qualified rather than vetoed because the Van der Speeten MMC pharmacokinetic argument was about mitomycin C, not oxaliplatin. The rank-4 row preserves the patient's surgical autonomy with mitomycin C as the lower-bad-choice perfusate if HIPEC is performed at all; this row exists to close the door explicitly on the oxaliplatin agent so the family conversation does not absorb a marketing claim that the trial data do not support.
likelihood_of_effect: None over CRS alone — PRODIGE 7 negative for OS; COLOPEC and PROPHYLOCHIP reinforce the negative.
toxicity_burden: High (60-day G3+ morbidity 25-40%, treatment-related mortality 1-3%; without OS benefit)

counter_productive_moa.description: Veto stands on mechanism: oxaliplatin HIPEC adds operative-window morbidity that delays systemic therapy without offsetting the patient with an OS gain.

overall: **Closed on randomized evidence — surgical team retains autonomy on HIPEC agent choice; oxaliplatin perfusate specifically should not be framed as OS-validated in the family conversation.**
